title: 2.3.29 Convert an if-chain to switch
description: Rewrite an if/else-if chain as a switch statement with at least two cases, a default, and break. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: practice converting an if/else-if chain to switch, ahead of 2.3.30 A2.3.1 Print Settings Advisor

steps.title: Create a variable to switch on
steps.instructions: Create a variable called day and assign it a day-of-week string, for example 'Monday'.

steps.title: Write a switch statement
steps.instructions: Write a switch statement that checks the value of day. Include at least two case labels (for example 'Monday' and 'Friday'), a default label, and a break statement after each case body. Inside each case, use console.log to print a message for that day.

requirements.title: case label present
requirements.description: A quoted case label is directly followed by a console.log call

requirements.title: default label present
requirements.description: The default label is directly followed by a console.log call

requirements.title: at least two breaks, one per case
requirements.description: Code contains at least two break statements, one after each case body.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code

Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
